source_text: Ἀλλὰ τὰ μὲν εἰς τὸν πάντων βασιλέα καὶ κηδεμόνα, τὴν διαρκῆ πηγὴν πάντων ἀγαθῶν, εὐφημίας καὶ ὕμνους, τῷ κἂν τούτῳ τὴν ἀσθένειαν ἡμῶν ἰωμένῳ, καὶ τὸ ἐνδέον ἀναπληροῦν μόνῳ δυναμένῳ ἐπιτρέψομεν, τῷ προστάτῃ τῶν ἡμετέρων ψυχῶν καὶ σωτῆρι, τῷ πρωτογενεῖ αὐτοῦ λόγῳ, τῷ πάντων δημιουργῷ καὶ κυβερνήτῃ, αὐτῷ μόνῳ ὑπέρ τε ἑαυτοῦ, καὶ ὑπὲρ πάντων ἰδίᾳ τε καὶ ἑκάστου, καὶ ἀθρόον ἅμα δυνατὸν ὂν ἀναπέμπειν διηνεκεῖς καὶ ἀδιαλείπτους τῷ πατρὶ τὰς εὐχαριστίας, ὅτι αὐτὸς ἡ ἀλήθεια ὢν, καὶ ἡ αὐτοῦ τοῦ πατρὸς τῶν ὅλων καὶ σοφία καὶ δύναμις· πρὸς δὲ, καὶ ἐν αὐτῷ ὢν καὶ πρὸς αὐτὸν ἀτεχνῶς ἡνωμένος, οὐκ ἔστιν ὅπως ἢ διὰ λήθην, ἢ ἀσοφίας, ἢ ὑπ᾽ ἀσθενείας τινὸς ὥσπερ τις ἀπεξενωμένος αὐτοῦ, ἢ οὐκ ἐφίξεται τῇ δυνάμει τῆς δυνάμεως, ἢ ἐφίξεται μὲν, ἑκὼν δὲ, ὃ μὴ θεμιτὸν εἰπεῖν, ἐάσῃ τὸν πατέρα ἀνευφήμητον· μόνῳ τούτῳ δυνατὸν ὂν τελεώτατα πᾶσαν ἀποπληρῶσαι τὴν ἀξίαν τῶν αὐτῷ προσηκόντων αἴνων· ὅν τινα αὐτὸς ὁ τῶν ὅλων πατὴρ ἓν πρὸς αὐτὸν ποιησάμενος, δι᾽ αὐτοῦ μονονουχὶ αὐτὸς αὐτὸν ἐκπεριιὼν, τῇ ἴσῃ πάντῃ δυνάμει τῇ αὐτοῦ τρόπον τινὰ τιμῶν καὶ τιμᾶται· ὅπερ πρῶτος καὶ μόνος, ἔχειν ἔλαχεν ἐκ πάντων τῶν ὄντων, ὁ μονογενὴς αὐτοῦ, ὁ ἐν αὐτῷ Θεὸς λόγος. τῶν ἄλλων πάντων οὕτω μόνον εὐχαρίστων καὶ εὐσεβῶν εἶναι δυναμένων, εἰ ἐπ᾽ αὐτῷ φέροντες μόνῳ ἀντὶ πάντων τῶν παρὰ τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῖν ἀγαθῶν, τὴν δύναμιν τῆς ἀξίας εὐχαριστίας ἀναθήσομεν· μίαν ὁδὸν εὐσεβείας ταύτην εἶναι ὁμολογήσαντες, τὴν δι᾽ αὐτοῦ πᾶσαν μνήμην, τῷ τῶν ὅλων αἰτίῳ. διὸ δὴ τῆς μὲν ἐπὶ πᾶσι διηνεκοῦς προνοίας, ἔν τε μεγίστοις καὶ ἐν τοῖς ἐλαχίστοις κηδομένης ἡμῶν, καὶ εἰς τοῦτό γε προηγμένης, ἐκεῖνος ἄξιος διηνεκὴς εἶναι λόγος εἰς εὐχαριστίας καὶ ὕμνους ὁμολογείσθω, τελειότατος ὢν καὶ ζῶν, καὶ αὐτοῦ τοῦ πρώτου νοῦ λόγος ἔμψυχος ὤν.
thought_title: Only the Word can give the Father worthy thanks
orientation: Gregory leaves the praise owed to the King of all to the Word, who alone can give the Father worthy thanks.
pass_a_gloss: But the praises and ὕμνοι to the King of all and guardian, the unfailing fountain of all goods, we shall entrust to the one even in this healing our weakness, and alone able to fill up what is lacking: to the protector of our souls and savior, to his firstborn Word, the maker and governor of all; to him alone it being possible, for himself and for all individually and each, and all together at once, to send up continual and unceasing εὐχαριστίαι to the Father; because he himself being the Truth, and the wisdom and power of the Father of all himself; besides, being in him and wholly united to him, there is no way that either through forgetfulness or lack of wisdom or by some ἀσθένεια, as one estranged from him, he either will not reach by power the power, or reaching, willingly — which is not lawful to say — leave the Father unpraised; to this one alone it being possible most perfectly to fulfill all the worth of the αἶνοι due to him; whom the Father of all himself having made one with himself, through him all but himself going round, encompassing himself, with power equal in every way of his own, in a way honoring is also honored; which first and alone of all beings obtained to have, his Only-begotten, the God Word in him. All others able to be thankful and pious only thus: if, bearing to him alone, in return for all the goods from the Father to us, we dedicate the δύναμις of worthy εὐχαριστία; confessing this to be one way of piety: all remembrance through him to the cause of all. Therefore for the providence unceasing over all, caring for us in greatest and least, and having advanced even to this, let it be confessed that he is worthy unceasing word/Word for εὐχαριστίαι and ὕμνοι, being most perfect and living, and ensouled, living Word of the First Mind himself.

pass_b_english: But the praises and hymns due to the King and Guardian of all, the unfailing fountain of all good things, we shall leave to him who heals our weakness even in this, and who alone can supply what is lacking: to the Protector and Savior of our souls, his firstborn Word, the Maker and Governor of all. He alone can send up to the Father unceasing and uninterrupted thanksgivings, both for himself and for all, for each one separately and for all together at once. For he is himself the Truth (John 14:6), and the Wisdom and Power of the very Father of all (1 Corinthians 1:24). Moreover, he is in the Father and wholly united to him, so there is no way that through forgetfulness, or lack of wisdom, or some weakness, as though he were a stranger to him, he should either fail to reach the Father's power with his own power, or reach it and yet willingly (which it is not lawful even to say) leave the Father unpraised.

He alone is able to fulfill most perfectly the full worth of the praises due to the Father. The Father of all himself has made him one with himself, and through him all but encompasses himself; honoring him in a way with a power equal in every respect to his own, he is himself honored. This, first and alone of all beings, his Only-begotten was given to have: God the Word who is in him (John 1:1). All others can be thankful and godly only in this way: if we ascribe to him alone, in return for all the good things we have from the Father, the power of worthy thanksgiving, confessing that this is the one way of godliness, that every remembrance of the Cause of all is made through him.

Therefore, for the unceasing providence over all things, which cares for us in the greatest things and in the least, and which has come even this far, let it be confessed that he is the worthy and unceasing Word of thanksgivings and hymns; for he is most perfect and living, the animate Word of the First Mind himself.
notes: Clear allusions cited inline: 'himself the Truth' (John 14:6); 'Wisdom and Power' of the Father (1 Corinthians 1:24, 'Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God'); 'God the Word who is in him' (John 1:1). 'His Only-begotten ... God the Word' may also echo John 1:18 (μονογενὴς θεός), and 'in him' John 10:38 or 14:10; left uncited as not certain. 'Protector and Savior of our souls' resembles 1 Peter 2:25 ('Shepherd and Overseer of your souls') but uses different words; not cited. 'Firstborn Word' renders πρωτογενὴς λόγος (not πρωτότοκος of Colossians 1:15); not cited. Agency kept in 'honoring him ... he is himself honored' (τιμῶν καὶ τιμᾶται): the Father honors the Son and is honored through him. 'All but encompasses himself' renders μονονουχὶ αὐτὸς αὐτὸν ἐκπεριιών literally; the Father, through the Son, as it were returns upon himself in praise. 'Through him' at the end of the second paragraph renders 'τὴν δι᾽ αὐτοῦ πᾶσαν μνήμην τῷ τῶν ὅλων αἰτίῳ'. In the last sentence λόγος plays on 'Word' and 'speech of thanks'; 'animate Word' renders λόγος ἔμψυχος ('ensouled Word') and 'First Mind' renders πρῶτος νοῦς, Gregory's philosophical name for the Father. 'Has come even this far' renders προηγμένης (Latin 'hucusque provecta est'). 'Godly/godliness' render εὐσεβής/εὐσέβεια. Gloss in the Latin margin at 'αὐτῷ μόνῳ' not translated.
